AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Card SELECTION is faithful (the last Basic-rarity deck card carrying each of the Strike and Defend tags), but the upgrade itself is `card.upgrade()` -- the sim's unguarded bare increment -- where C# routes through CardCmd.Upgrade, which SKIPS a card that is already at its MaxUpgradeLevel.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): unguarded Card.upgrade() -- an already-upgraded last Basic Strike or Defend is pushed to upgrade_level 2, past its max_upgrade_level of 1
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `CardCmd.upgrade(hooks, card)` exists (cmds.py) and is CardCmd.cs:265-290's per-card body: the verb sits inside `if (!IsEnding)` and skips any card whose `IsUpgradable` is false, i.e. `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-789). 35 of the 203 ported cards are at MaxUpgradeLevel 0 (18 Curse, 14 Status, 3 Quest), and C# THROWS if CurrentUpgradeLevel is ever set above MaxUpgradeLevel (CardModel.cs:773-776) -- so the bare `card.upgrade()` was producing a state the source treats as impossible, and one conformance compares against the save as an (id, upgrade_level) pair. neows_talisman.py routes both Basic picks through it. EXECUTED: with the deck's last Basic Strike and Defend already smithed, both stay at 1 where they used to reach 2 and then read `is_upgradable` False.  Pinned by test/test_procure_and_upgrade_verbs.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: CardCmd.Upgrade(IEnumerable) opens with `if (!card.IsUpgradable) continue;` (CardCmd.cs:271-276), and IsUpgradable is `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-795) -- C# additionally THROWS if CurrentUpgradeLevel is ever set above MaxUpgradeLevel (CardModel.cs:773-776), so the state the sim produces is one the source treats as impossible. neows_talisman.py:32 calls `card.upgrade()`, which is a bare `self.upgrade_level += 1` (cards/base.py:146-148) with no filter. This is PROMPT.md bug class 14 and is the third of Sweep D's three unaudited unguarded sites (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md, `neows_talisman.py:29 after_obtained`) -- confirmed here, not re-derived. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py neows-talisman): with the deck's last Basic Strike and last Basic Defend already at level 1, the relic takes both to level 2 and `is_upgradable` then reads False on both; C# leaves both at 1. REACHABILITY (LIVE, and it took work, because Neow's Talisman is only granted at floor 0 where the deck is pristine): relic/neows_bones grants TWO relics from the same Neow option pool IN SEQUENCE (neows_bones.py:28-29), and relic/pomander -- 'upgrade a chosen card' (pomander.py:14-16) -- is in that pool. Executed: `pomander` and `neows_talisman` are both in neow_relic_pool, string seed B10BONES0136 makes Neow's Bones grant pomander FIRST and neows_talisman second, and running that exact pair through add_relic with a selector that picks the last Basic Strike produces ('strike', 2) where C# produces ('strike', 1). The observable is not cosmetic: conformance/runner.py compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs, and an over-upgraded Strike also prints wrong damage. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, cards/base.py, relics/neows_bones.py, relics/pomander.py, events/neow.py, conformance/runner.py and the sweeps document are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `source.LastOrDefault(c => c.Tags.Contains(CardTag.Strike))` over Basic-rarity DECK cards (NeowsTalisman.cs:18-23)
guards.rationale: EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py neows-talisman): on a clean 5-Strike/4-Defend deck the relic upgrades exactly the fifth Strike and the fourth Defend, i.e. the LAST of each. _basic_with_tag(deck, tag, last=True) (neows_talisman.py:6-16) applies the same CardRarity.BASIC filter and the same tag membership test and returns matches[-1]. The null case matches too: C#'s LastOrDefault yields null and the foreach skips it (NeowsTalisman.cs:26-29); the sim returns None and skips at neows_talisman.py:31.

guards.what: N2: C# materialises BOTH LastOrDefault results into an array BEFORE upgrading either (NeowsTalisman.cs:19-23); the sim evaluates and upgrades one tag at a time (neows_talisman.py:30-32)
guards.rationale: Checked deliberately, because interleaving a mutation with a search is exactly where an order bug hides. Upgrading a card changes neither its CardRarity, nor its Tags, nor its position in the deck, and no ported Basic card carries both the Strike and the Defend tag (they are the tags on Strike and Defend), so the two searches are independent and the two orders coincide.

guards.what: N3: CardCmd.Upgrade's other two side effects -- the `CombatManager.Instance.IsEnding` early return (CardCmd.cs:267-270) and the CurrentMapPointHistoryEntry.UpgradedCards bookkeeping (CardCmd.cs:277-281)
guards.rationale: The IsEnding return is a mid-combat-teardown guard and this hook is an out-of-combat pickup, so it cannot be reached; UpgradedCards is the game's own save/replay bookkeeping, which the sim's conformance layer READS out of the save (the oracle) rather than writes. Neither can change a game state either codebase can observe. Waived under the presentation/out-of-scope-machinery exclusion rather than on an unreachability claim about ported content. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs is unhashed here.
